grade_rationale.text: Machal names the water-spirit for the Russians, Bohemians, Slovenians and Poles.
Machal records the Ukrainians burying a horse's head in a dam to keep the Vodyanik from destroying it.
Ralston describes the Vodyany from Russian peasant belief and gives a Bohemian telling, without citing Afanasyev on those passages.
Ralston's drowned-girl story cites Afanasyev (P. V. S. II. 239), so on that passage he is not independent of Afanasyev.
Afanasyev records the vodyanoi among the Lusatians, in Little Russia and among the Czechs of Bohemia, as well as in Rus'.
Machal, Ralston and Afanasyev are three independent authors attesting it across six verified peoples (Russians, Czechs, Slovenes, Poles, Ukrainians, Sorbs).
